If the shell now undergoes an adiabatic expansion the relation between $T$ and $R$ is:

Two particles $A$ and $B$ of equal mass $M$ are moving with the same speed $v$ as shown in the figure. They collide completely inelastically and move as a single particle $C$. The angle $\theta$ that the path of $C$ makes with the $X$-axis is given by:

figure_refs.caption: Two particles A and B moving at angles 30° and 45° to the X-axis, colliding to form particle C at angle theta
figure_refs.alt_text: A coordinate system with X and Y axes. Particle A moves upward and to the right at 30 degrees to the positive X-axis. Particle B moves downward and to the left at 45 degrees below the negative X-axis. Particle C moves upward to the right at angle theta to the positive X-axis after the collision.

statement: Figure shows a network of capacitors where the numbers indicate capacitances in micro Farad. The value of capacitance $C$ if the equivalent capacitance between point $A$ and $B$ is to be $1\text{ }\mu\text{F}$ is:

figure_refs.caption: Network of capacitors with values C, 1, 8, 2, 2, 12, 6, 4 μF between terminals A and B
figure_refs.alt_text: A complex capacitor network between points A (left) and B (right). From A, the circuit splits into upper and lower branches. The upper branch has capacitor C in series with 1 μF. From the junction after C, 8 μF goes down and 6 μF goes right to a node connecting to 4 μF going to B. The lower branch from A has 2 μF, then from that junction 2 μF goes right, and 12 μF connects between middle nodes. The network forms a bridge-like structure.
